theater: 南義大利與西西里戰線

battle.name: 皮洛士戰爭
battle.theater: 南義大利與西西里戰線
battle.brief: 前280年春天，伊庇魯斯王皮洛士率二萬兵與二十頭象自塔蘭圖姆登陸義大利，在赫拉克萊亞擊潰羅馬執政官軍，開啟這場歷時五年的戰爭；皮洛士連勝四場卻耗盡家底。卡面的亞述長弓是對照件：複合弓技術經波斯傳入希臘，落地成為此役希臘、伊利里亞與西西里弓手所用的短弓。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 皮洛士戰爭（前280年至前275年）是羅馬共和國與伊庇魯斯王國之間的戰爭，戰場在亞平寧山以南的南義大利，並延伸到西西里島。交戰的一方是羅馬共和國：最高決策在元老院，戰場指揮由兩位執政官分掌，各帶一個軍團式的步兵核心與約三百騎兵的羅馬騎兵，輔以拉丁同盟與各意大利盟邦的步兵，並僱用希臘、伊利里亞與色雷斯的弓手與投槍手；元老院在前280年拒絕議和，在前278年批准攻勢與追擊。另一方是伊庇魯斯王皮洛士的聯軍：核心是馬其頓式重步兵方陣，配伊利里亞長矛兵、色雷斯兵與五百名克里特弓手，騎兵包含希臘雇傭騎兵、達爾達尼亞騎兵與塔蘭圖姆提供的塔蘭提姆騎兵，最關鍵的是二十頭象；義大利境內的塔蘭圖姆、洛西里與墨薩比安人站在他這一邊。第三方是迦太基：它先在敘拉古一線與皮洛士對抗，卻在前279年轉而與羅馬締約，把西西里與地中海的形勢交到羅馬手裡。羅馬與皮洛士之間還夾著薩莫尼特人、坎帕尼亞人與赫爾尼基人，前278年一批薩莫尼特傭兵在牛喉峽被羅馬殲滅，皮洛士在南義大利的地盤迅速縮小。
countriesEn: The Pyrrhic War (280–275 BC) was fought between the Roman Republic and the kingdom of Epirus, in the part of Italy south of the Apennines and on Sicily. One side was the Roman Republic: the highest decisions were taken in the Senate, while command in the field was shared by two consuls, each with a legionary core of infantry and about three hundred Roman cavalry, supported by the Latin League and the troops of the Italian allies, with Greek, Illyrian and Thracian archers and javelin-throwers taken into pay; the Senate refused terms of peace in 280 BC and authorised the offensive and the pursuit in 278 BC. The other side was the coalition of King Pyrrhus of Epirus: at its core a Macedonian-style phalanx of heavy infantry, with Illyrian pikemen, Thracians and five hundred Cretan archers, cavalry made up of Greek mercenary horse, Dardanian riders and Tarentine cavalry supplied by Tarentum, and above all twenty war elephants; on the Italian side Tarentum, Locri and the Messapians stood with him. The third party was Carthage: it fought Pyrrhus around Syracuse at first, but in 279 BC turned to a treaty with Rome, handing the initiative in Sicily and the Mediterranean to the Romans. Between Rome and Pyrrhus also stood the Samnites, Campanians and Hernici; a body of Samnite mercenaries was annihilated by Rome in the Caudine Forks in 278 BC, and Pyrrhus's footing in southern Italy shrank quickly as a result.
people: 皮洛士本人是伊庇魯斯阿基里王朝的成員，幼年流亡在外，後來在亞歷山大大帝的軍中受訓，前283年前後返國即位，前281年以援助塔蘭圖姆的名義進入義大利；娶敘拉古僭主阿伽托克勒斯的女兒蘭薩莎作聯姻，洛西里把赫拉克萊亞城與土地作為聘禮送給他，等於替他備好進軍的跳板。軍中最受信任的將領是亞歷山德羅·皮德納，他率領希臘雇傭騎兵與克里特弓手，羅馬人稱其為全軍最精銳的騎將；皮洛士的兒子托勒密則在前275年的最終決戰中陣亡。皮洛士本人迷信占卜，出征前屢次詢問神諭，這在當時被視為軟弱。羅馬方面的關鍵人物先是前280年的兩位執政官提比里烏斯·科倫卡尼烏斯與蓋烏斯·法布里基烏斯，前者是第一個迎上皮洛士的羅馬將軍，後者以平民出身的誠實著稱，據說拒絕了皮洛士的巨額賄賂；同年的監察官阿皮烏斯·克勞狄烏斯·凱庫斯在元老院發表反對議和的演說，是否掉和約的關鍵一票。據普魯塔克記載，議場上主張交涉者以法布里基烏斯最有名，主張不應讓步者則包括老西庇阿與昆圖斯·塞爾維利烏斯。前279年追擊皮洛士的是執政官昆圖斯·法比烏斯·馬克西穆斯·魯利安努斯與昆圖斯·塞爾維利烏斯；前278年擊敗皮洛士的是馬爾庫斯·庫里烏斯·登塔圖斯，他以執政官身分要求皮洛士無條件撤出義大利，同僚盧基烏斯·帕皮里烏斯·庫爾索在牛喉峽殲滅薩莫尼特傭兵；前275年作出決定性一擊的是執政官蓋烏斯·斯克里波尼烏斯·庫里奧，而主張延後進攻、強調操練對付象兵的蓋烏斯·法比烏斯·馬克西穆斯被後人稱為遲疑者。迦太基方面則是敘拉古前線的哈米爾卡與漢尼拔·吉斯可。史料上，波里比俄斯的《歷史》第二卷是本役最重要的一手記述，普魯塔克《皮洛士傳》提供道德化的細節，李維的戰史提要補上編年框架。
peopleEn: Pyrrhus himself was a member of the Aeacid dynasty of Epirus, exiled as a boy and later trained in the army of Alexander the Great; he returned to his kingdom around 283 BC and entered Italy in 281 BC as the helper of Tarentum. He married Lanassa, daughter of the Syracusan tyrant Agathocles, and the Locrians handed him the city of Heraclea and land as a dowry, which gave him both a springboard and a base for his advance. The officer he trusted most was Alexander of Pydna, who commanded the Greek mercenary cavalry and the Cretan archers and was described by the Romans as the finest horseman in the host; Pyrrhus's son Ptolemy was killed in the last decisive battle of the war, in 275 BC. Pyrrhus was himself given to divination and consulted the oracles repeatedly before campaigning, which his contemporaries read as a weakness. The decisive figures on the Roman side began with the two consuls of 280 BC, Tiberius Coruncanius and Gaius Fabricius, the first being the Roman general to meet Pyrrhus and the second a man of plebeian origin famous for his honesty, who is said to have refused Pyrrhus's enormous bribe; the censor of the same year, Appius Claudius Caecus, delivered the speech in the Senate that killed the peace terms, and his was the decisive vote. Plutarch records that Fabricius was the most famous advocate of negotiation, while the men who argued that no concession should be made included the elder Scipio and Quintus Servilius. The consuls who pursued Pyrrhus in 279 BC were Quintus Fabius Maximus Rullianus and Quintus Servilius; the man who beat Pyrrhus in 278 BC was Marcus Curius Dentatus, who as consul demanded an unconditional withdrawal from Italy, while his colleague Lucius Papirius Cursor annihilated the Samnite mercenaries in the Caudine Forks; the decisive blow of 275 BC was struck by the consul Gaius Scribonius Curio, while Gaius Fabius Maximus, who argued for delay and for drilling the troops against the elephants, was afterwards called the Delayer. On the Carthaginian side were Hamilcar and Hannibal Gisco in front of Syracuse. For sources, Book 2 of Polybius is the principal first-hand account, Plutarch's Life of Pyrrhus supplies the moralised detail, and the epitomes of Livius supply the chronological frame.
kits: 卡面是亞述長弓：公元前七世紀中葉亞述王國的短型複合弓，弓臂以木、骨、筋合成，配短箭；亞述人靠弓與鐵的組合征服兩河流域，弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路，車上射手與步行射手分工明確，投射火力是全軍的骨架。所以這件兵器在皮洛士戰爭裡的位置是對照件，而不是戰場實物：前280年的亞平寧山南岸沒有亞述弓。可對照的是同出一源的分弓，就是所謂佩萊基斯（pelekys），行家常稱的托克索特斯即以此弓配箭袋（gorytos）射擊，箭長約六十至七十厘米；它承自波斯與西徐亞一系，而亞述的弓術正是經波斯傳承下來，亞歷山大東征之後成為希臘化世界的標準投射兵器。皮洛士的軍中有五百名克里特弓手與色雷斯弓手，羅馬軍中的弓手則來自希臘、伊利里亞與色雷斯的傭兵；羅馬公民兵團本身更倚重重標槍與短劍，弓並非羅馬的看家本領，專職弓箭兵要到更晚才成型。另一條對照線是亞述的車：亞述軍以車載弓兵破陣，到前280年希臘的戰車已退出戰鬥編制，只餘儀仗與婚禮之用，皮洛士改用大象承擔同一個角色，以體量與異獸製造恐慌、衝亂敵陣，赫拉克萊亞一役羅馬全軍正是被象與隨後的騎兵切斷。雙方其餘裝備的差異同樣明顯：皮洛士用馬其頓式方陣的重裝備與希臘式圓盾，羅馬用弧面大盾（scutum）、短劍與重標槍，並靠營地壕溝木柵、配重石弩與投石機攻城；皮洛士的攻城器材遠不如羅馬，攻不下羅馬同盟的城市，這正是他最後輸在補給與攻城能力上的根源。
kitsEn: The card shows the Assyrian bow: a short composite bow of the mid seventh century BC, its limbs built up from wood, horn and sinew, fired with short arrows. The Assyrians conquered the river valleys of Mesopotamia with the combination of bow and iron; their archers shot from chariots, and the chariots depended on the archers to open the way, with mounted and foot archers given separate tasks, and the volleys of the bow were the skeleton of the whole army. The weapon's place in the Pyrrhic War is therefore as a reference piece and not as a piece actually present: there were no Assyrian bows south of the Apennines in 280 BC. The piece it can be compared with is a bow of the same composite family, the so-called pelekys, which the toxotes carried with a gorytos and fired with arrows roughly sixty to seventy centimetres long; it descended from the Persian and Scythian line, and the Assyrian archery had reached the Greeks by way of Persia, becoming the standard missile weapon of the Hellenistic world after Alexander's campaign in Asia. Pyrrhus's army had five hundred Cretan archers and Thracian archers, while the archers in the Roman army were Greek, Illyrian and Thracian mercenaries; the Roman citizen infantry relied far more on the heavy pilum and the gladius, and the bow was never the Roman strong suit, specialist archers emerging much later. A second line of comparison is the Assyrian chariot: the Assyrian army broke formations with chariot-borne archers, and by 280 BC the Greek war chariot had left the order of battle altogether, surviving only in pageantry and wedding processions, so Pyrrhus assigned the same role to the elephant, using bulk and a foreign animal to create panic and to break up enemy formations; at Heraclea it was the elephants and the cavalry that followed them that cut the Roman army in two. The differences in the rest of the equipment are equally clear: Pyrrhus had the heavy kit of the Macedonian phalanx and the Greek round shield, Rome had the curved oval scutum, the gladius and the heavy pilum, and brought to bear the ditch, palisade and camp of the Roman marching camp together with torsion stone-throwers and ballistae in siege; Pyrrhus's siege equipment was far inferior, he could not take the allied cities of Rome, and that is the root of the defeat he finally suffered on supply and on siege capability.
tactics: 波里比俄斯留下的戰術描寫是本役最珍貴的技術資料。赫拉克萊亞之役，羅馬以約六千步兵與八百騎兵擋住皮洛士約二萬步兵、三千騎兵與二十頭象；皮洛士把象與最精銳的兵放在兩翼，羅馬人見象而懼，中央的守軍自行退向兩翼山地，中央陣線就這樣被撕開，方陣並不正面硬撞，而在缺口出現後從側面切進，把羅馬中軍包住吃掉——羅馬人不是被正面打敗，是自己放棄了正面。追擊戰是第二關：前279年皮洛士率軍追入亞布里亞，兩位執政官不與他正面交鋒，只退入沼澤與城邑消耗他、避其銳氣，雨季、飢病與行軍距離拖垮了追兵，最終在一處河谷決戰，羅馬仍然損失慘重，卻沒有被全殲。真正決定走向的是前279年秋的阿斯庫盧姆之役：羅馬佔據山丘上的營地，皮洛士強攻不下，雙方在丘陵上反覆拉鋸，最後皮洛士主動撤收兵營，甚至放棄收埋羅馬陣亡者的屍體，因為他正在寫信給元老院求和——贏了戰場，卻把戰爭的主動權交了出去，這正是皮洛士式勝利的原型。前278年貝內文圖姆，執政官庫里烏斯·登塔圖斯據城固守、夜襲皮洛士營寨成功，使皮洛士退回塔蘭圖姆；同年盧基烏斯·帕皮里烏斯·庫爾索在牛喉峽以伏擊全滅薩莫尼特傭兵，切斷皮洛士在南義大利的徵召來源。前275年布圖利亞，據波里比俄斯殘存的記述與後世史家的推斷，羅馬執政官斯克里波尼烏斯·庫里奧不與象正面對撞，而以騎兵繞到象陣與步兵的側後攻擊其無防部位，皮洛士的行列被切斷，兒子托勒密陣亡，戰局崩解。整體看，這是一場以時間與城市換戰場的戰爭：羅馬以執政官輪換、同盟城市與海運補給耗損對方，皮洛士則靠劫掠與一次次的野戰勝利維持一支越來越難以補給的軍隊。
tacticsEn: The tactical description left by Polybius is the most valuable technical record of the war. At Heraclea, some six thousand foot and eight hundred horse faced about twenty thousand foot, three thousand horse and twenty elephants; Pyrrhus put the elephants and his best troops on the wings, the Romans were frightened by the elephants, and the troops in the centre withdrew of their own accord towards the hills on the wings, so that the centre of the line was torn open; the phalanx did not strike head-on but came round through the gap and closed around the Roman centre, which was destroyed — the Romans were not beaten in front, they gave up the front themselves. The pursuit was the second test: in 279 BC Pyrrhus followed them into Apulia, the two consuls refused to give battle, falling back into marshes and fortified towns to wear him down and blunt his edge, and the rainy season, sickness and the length of the marches exhausted the pursuers; the armies finally fought in a river valley, where the Romans still suffered heavily but were not annihilated. What really decided the course was the battle of Asculum in the autumn of 279 BC: the Romans held a camp on a hill, Pyrrhus could not take it by assault, the two sides fought back and forth over the broken ground, and at last Pyrrhus withdrew of his own will, leaving even the Roman dead unburied, because he was at that moment writing to the Senate to ask for terms — he won the field and handed the initiative of the war back to the enemy, which is the prototype of the Pyrrhic victory. In 278 BC at Beneventum the consul Curius Dentatus held his city, raided Pyrrhus's camp by night with success and forced him back to Tarentum; in the same year Lucius Papirius Cursor annihilated the Samnite mercenaries in an ambush in the Caudine Forks, cutting off Pyrrhus's source of recruits in southern Italy. In 275 BC in Bruttium, on the fragment of Polybius and the reconstruction of later historians, the Roman consul Scribonius Curio did not charge the elephants head-on but took his cavalry round to the flank and rear of the elephant line and the foot, where there was no defence; Pyrrhus's line was cut, his son Ptolemy fell, and the battle collapsed. Taken as a whole this was a war in which time and cities were exchanged for battlefields: Rome wore the enemy down with the rotation of the consuls, the allied cities and sea-borne supply, while Pyrrhus tried to sustain an army that grew harder to supply on plunder and on a series of field victories.
data: 留下數字的地方主要在波里比俄斯《歷史》第二卷。赫拉克萊亞一役，羅馬方面的兵力是步兵約六千、騎兵約八百（其中羅馬騎兵約六百、坎帕尼亞騎兵約二百），皮洛士方面是步兵約二萬（方陣重步兵約八千，另有伊利里亞長矛兵、色雷斯兵與五百克里特弓手）、騎兵約三千（希臘雇傭騎兵約一千、達爾達尼亞騎兵約三百、塔蘭提姆騎兵約二千）、象二十頭。戰果方面，波里比俄斯記載赫拉克萊亞一役羅馬人陣亡約一千二百至一千四百人、被俘約二千人，皮洛士一方只損失數百人與數頭象；前279年追擊戰羅馬方面再損失約二千人陣亡、約一千四百人被俘；前278年貝內文圖姆與牛喉峽兩役，羅馬又殲滅大批薩莫尼特傭兵與皮洛士的攻城部隊。概括性的數字出自普魯塔克《皮洛士傳》結尾：皮洛士在義大利共打了六場仗，贏了四場，最後仍敗於羅馬之手；他給出的雙方總損失常被引述為羅馬約二萬人、皮洛士約四千人，這是文學性的總結而非逐戰帳目，但方向明確：義大利的戰場是羅馬用兵源與城市換來的。時間上，本役自前280年打到前275年，義大利的戰役歷經五個年度，中間插入前278年至前275年皮洛士轉赴西西里作戰的兩年。距離上，軍隊自塔蘭圖姆南下赫拉克萊亞約兩百公里，北抵貝內文圖姆，再轉戰布圖利亞，全線超過四百公里；羅馬的補給靠海運與阿庇亞大道維持，皮洛士則靠劫掠城邑現取現用。象是可追蹤的損失項：二十頭象中大部分在西西里與迦太基的衝突中耗損，返回義大利時所剩無幾，這也是前275年之戰中象兵威勢大不如前的原因。
dataEn: The numbers survive mainly in Book 2 of Polybius. At Heraclea the Roman force was about six thousand foot and eight hundred horse, of which roughly six hundred were Roman cavalry and two hundred Campanian, against about twenty thousand foot, three thousand horse and twenty elephants on the Pyrrhic side, the foot including eight thousand in the phalanx, Illyrian pikemen, Thracians and five hundred Cretan archers, and the three thousand horse including about a thousand Greek mercenaries, three hundred Dardanians and two thousand Tarentines. On results, Polybius records that at Heraclea the Romans lost about twelve hundred to fourteen hundred men killed and about two thousand taken prisoner, while Pyrrhus lost only a few hundred men and a few elephants; in the pursuit of 279 BC the Romans lost about two thousand more killed and about fourteen hundred captured; and in 278 BC the battles of Beneventum and the Caudine Forks destroyed a further body of Samnite mercenaries and Pyrrhus's siege troops. The summarizing figure comes from the close of Plutarch's Life of Pyrrhus: Pyrrhus fought six battles in Italy and won four of them, and was nonetheless beaten by Rome in the end; the total losses he gives for the two sides, commonly quoted as some twenty thousand men for Rome against about four thousand for Pyrrhus, are a literary summation rather than a battle-by-battle ledger, but their direction is clear: the battlefield in Italy was bought by Rome with man-power and with cities. In time the war ran from 280 to 275 BC, with five campaigning years in Italy and the two years from 278 to 275 spent by Pyrrhus in Sicily. In distance the armies covered some two hundred kilometres from Tarentum down to Heraclea, pushed north to Beneventum and then turned back to Bruttium, a front of more than four hundred kilometres in all; Rome kept itself supplied by sea and by the Via Appia, while Pyrrhus lived off the plunder of towns as he went. The elephants are a loss that can be followed: most of the twenty were worn out or destroyed in the fighting in Sicily against Carthage, and very few were brought back to Italy, which is why the elephants played so much smaller a part in 275 BC than before.
cause: 打起來的原因是三層。外層是羅馬在南義大利的擴張：前280年前後羅馬剛以薩莫尼特戰爭解決了內陸的薩莫尼特人，把南義大利的希臘城市編入自己的同盟體系，希臘城邦對羅馬的戒心與恐懼由此積累。直接導火索在東邊：塔蘭圖姆擔心羅馬的盟友圖里伊與墨薩比安人威脅自己的商路與城邑，前281年請伊庇魯斯王皮洛士出兵；皮洛士以盟友身分率軍進入義大利，前280年塔蘭圖姆正式要求他對付羅馬，而洛西里把赫拉克萊亞城與土地作為聘禮送給皮洛士，等於替他備好進軍的跳板與補給基地。皮洛士本人的算盤同樣清楚：他需要戰利品養軍，需要在希臘世界重建自己的聲望，也需要一場勝利證明自己值得希臘城邦倚重；前281年他在義大利對墨薩比安人取勝並索取酬金，已顯示他並不打算只做一個聽命盟友。羅馬這邊不能容忍一個帶象的希臘王國插手亞平寧山以南，否則南義大利的同盟城市將整批倒向對手，羅馬的霸權與糧道同時受威脅；何況迦太基與皮洛士的接近已被視為同一條線上的事，羅馬不能讓兩邊站到一起。希臘聯盟本身的失敗是最後一層：敘拉古、洛西里等城各自求援而沒有共同計畫，皮洛士的聯軍看似強大，卻沒有能持續作戰的後勤體系，也沒有第二支可以接替的軍隊。
causeEn: There were three layers of cause. The outer one was the Roman expansion into southern Italy: in the years around 280 BC Rome had just settled the Samnite question in the interior and drawn the Greek cities of southern Italy into its system of alliances, and the suspicion and fear of Rome in the Greek cities accumulated as a result. The immediate spark lay further east: Tarentum, worried that the allies and neighbours of Rome — Thurii and the Messapians — threatened its trade routes and its own city, called on Pyrrhus, king of Epirus, to bring troops in 281 BC; Pyrrhus entered Italy in the guise of an ally, and in 280 BC Tarentum formally asked him to turn against Rome, while the Locrians handed him the city of Heraclea and land as a dowry, which gave him a springboard and a supply base for his advance. Pyrrhus's own calculation was equally clear: he needed plunder to feed his army, he needed to rebuild his standing in the Greek world, and he needed a victory to show that the Greek cities were right to rely on him; his victory over the Messapians in 281 BC and his demand for payment had already shown that he did not mean to remain a client obeying orders. Rome could not tolerate a Greek kingdom with war elephants interfering south of the Apennines, or the allied cities of the south would go over to the enemy in a body and both Roman hegemony and Roman lines of supply would be threatened at once; and the approach of Carthage to Pyrrhus was already treated as part of the same business, so Rome could not let the two sides stand together. The failure of the Greek coalition is the last layer: Syracuse, Locri and the other cities each petitioned for help without any common plan, and Pyrrhus's confederation, imposing as it looked, had neither a logistic system capable of sustained campaigning nor a second army to relieve the first.
impact: 這場戰爭的影響，一半在戰場之外。制度層面，羅馬第一次以執政官輪換與城市同盟的辦法頂住了一支職業化程度更高的敵軍：羅馬不在每一場會戰裡求取全勝，而是把執政官的任期當作年度單位，把每次敗仗的損失視為可以再補充的消耗；這套邏輯後來在第二次馬其頓戰爭、第三次布匿戰與對抗捷林古人的戰爭裡被反覆使用，最後定型為羅馬的長期戰爭機器。地中海格局方面，皮洛士把迦太基推到羅馬這一邊，前279年的羅馬—迦太基條約讓羅馬在西西里取得港口、經費與盟邦的合法性，為前264年第一次布匿戰埋下伏筆；而羅馬正是在對付迦太基的戰爭中第一次自己出動象兵，北非的象兵是前275年那場教訓的直接回聲。希臘世界方面，皮洛士的失敗使希臘城邦對羅馬的恐懼與屈從同時加深，希臘人指望的獨立最後落空；但波里比俄斯在《歷史》第二卷裡為羅馬辯護，強調羅馬帶來的是秩序而非奴役，這一說法此後成為羅馬對希臘世界的自我說明，並被拉丁與歐洲的政治家沿用。文化層面更為持久：普魯塔克《皮洛士傳》結語所說的那個意思——用慘勝換來的勝利不叫勝利——從此成為皮洛士式勝利一語的來源，歐洲多種語言都拿它形容得不償失的成果；皮洛士本人也進入歐洲的政治與軍事傳說，希臘人與拉丁人寫他，一半寫他的天才，一半寫他的耗費。
impactEn: Half the consequences of this war lie off the battlefield. At the level of institutions, Rome held off a more professionally organised enemy for the first time by rotating the consuls and leaning on its network of allied cities: Rome did not seek total victory in every pitched battle, but treated the consular year as its unit of time and each defeat as a loss that could be made good again in replacements. That logic was used again in the Second Macedonian War, the Third Punic War and the war against the Celts, and it hardened into the Roman machine for long war. In the geography of the Mediterranean, Pyrrhus pushed Carthage into the arms of Rome, and the treaty of 279 BC gave Rome ports, money and standing among the allies in Sicily, planting the seed of the First Punic War declared in 264 BC; and it was in the war against Carthage that Rome first fielded elephants of its own, the North African elephant being the direct echo of the lesson of 275 BC. For the Greek world, Pyrrhus's defeat deepened Greek fear and Greek submission to Rome at the same time, and the independence the Greek cities had hoped for died out; but Polybius, writing Book 2, defended Rome by insisting that what Rome brought was order rather than servitude, and that argument became the Roman self-description to the Greek world and was later taken up by Latin and European politicians alike. The cultural effect is the most durable of all: the sense conveyed at the close of Plutarch's Life of Pyrrhus, that a victory bought at such a price is not a victory, gave rise to the term Pyrrhic victory, which several European languages still use for gains that cost more than they yield; and Pyrrhus himself entered European political and military legend, the Greeks and the Latin writing him half as a talent and half as an expenditure.
result: 結局是皮洛士的聯軍解體。前275年布圖利亞之役，執政官斯克里波尼烏斯·庫里奧的羅馬軍擊敗皮洛士，其子托勒密陣亡，殘部退回塔蘭圖姆；皮洛士放棄義大利，經海路撤回希臘。羅馬沒有在義大利誅滅一支軍隊，而是像處理任何一個被擊退的盟邦那樣，把塔蘭圖姆與其他希臘城市改組為自己的同盟，讓殘餘的伊庇魯斯傭兵解散。皮洛士回到伊庇魯斯後仍是一位強勢的君主，他轉而投向東地中海的希臘化國家，先後在敘拉古與亞該亞同盟的戰線上指揮作戰，前272年在亞爾戈斯戰死。對南義大利而言，這場戰爭的直接結果是羅馬完成了對亞平寧山以南的直接統治：義大利的城市網、拉丁同盟的兵源與新建的道路把這個半島變成羅馬的後院，也讓羅馬可以把注意力轉向海面。戰術上的結論則被後人記得更久：象可以被繞開與分割，野戰的勝負可以被城市、補給與輪換消耗慢慢扭轉，而任何一位靠一場場慘勝維持的入侵者，最後都會在兵源與補給上先耗盡自己。普魯塔克的結語並不停留在誰贏誰輸，而是指出雙方都已耗盡：羅馬拿到了戰場以外的一切，皮洛士只帶走了戰場上的名聲。
resultEn: The outcome was the disintegration of the Pyrrhic coalition. In the battle in Bruttium in 275 BC the Roman army of the consul Gaius Scribonius Curio defeated Pyrrhus, his son Ptolemy was killed, and the remnants fell back to Tarentum; Pyrrhus gave up Italy and sailed home to Greece. Rome did not destroy an army in Italy; it dealt with Tarentum and the other Greek cities as it dealt with any beaten ally, reorganising them into its own system of alliances and disbanding the surviving Epirote mercenaries. Back in Epirus, Pyrrhus remained a powerful ruler, turned eastward to the Hellenistic powers, and commanded in the war against Syracuse and in the fighting against the Achaean League, dying at Argos in 272 BC. For southern Italy the direct result of the war was the completion of Roman dominion south of the Apennines: the network of Italian cities, the man-power of the Latin League and the newly built roads turned the peninsula into Rome's backyard and freed Roman attention for the sea. The tactical conclusion was remembered far longer: elephants can be flanked and cut apart, the result of a field battle can be slowly reversed by cities, supply and rotation, and any invader who maintains himself on a series of costly victories will exhaust his own men-power and stores first. Plutarch's close does not stop at who won and who lost but notes that both sides were spent: Rome got everything there was to be got off the battlefield, and Pyrrhus carried away the name of his victories.
